cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've torn the prize cheque like you tore yours. Do you want to keep the money or pay for the team trip?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tore off a bank receipt. You've torn the cheque in half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, dividing the amount. Which half are we asking them to replace?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll replace the whole cheque. We could keep half and take a cheaper trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the team we're cutting the trip to keep half the prize. Is that what you want them to hear?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a torn receipt as prize division; B2 reveals a damaged cheque and A3 pretends physical halves are allocation. A5 makes B own the tradeoff in a cheaper trip.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 torn cheque leads A3 half replacement; B4 whole replacement/half kept leads A5 explicit reduced-trip announcement.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers a repair and compromise, giving B a problem-solving stance.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 solution to demand a public acknowledgment of what is being sacrificed.
